messages.content: In three sentences, explain why the sky is blue, then give the boiling point of water at sea level in both Celsius and Fahrenheit.

message.content: The sky appears blue because molecules in Earth’s atmosphere scatter shorter‑wavelength sunlight more efficiently than longer wavelengths, so when we look up we see the scattered blue light dominating. At sea level, pure water boils at 100 °C. This temperature corresponds to 212 °F, the standard conversion for water’s boiling point under normal atmospheric pressure.
